explain.say: Picture a giant dam holding back a lake. The wall is thin at the top but hugely thick at the bottom. Why build it that way? Because water pushes harder the deeper you go. Let us dive down and see.

explain.say: Deeper, yes! At 10 metres down, the weight of the water above adds about as much again as all the air above us. You can feel it in your ears at the bottom of a deep pool. More water on top means more pressure.

faq.q: Why is pressure low near the surface?
faq.a: Near the surface there is very little water above pressing down, so only air pressure acts.
asks: Why is water pressure small at the top?

faq.q: Why does water pressure increase with depth?
faq.a: The deeper you go, the more water there is above you, and its weight presses down harder on every square metre.
asks: Why is a dam wider at the bottom?

faq.q: What is the formula for pressure in a liquid?
faq.a: Pressure equals depth times density times g, written p = hρg. For water, every 10 metres adds about 100 kilopascals.

faq.q: Why do my ears hurt at the bottom of a pool?
faq.a: The water pressure outside your eardrum is bigger than the air pressure inside, so the eardrum is pushed inwards.

faq.q: Does the shape of the container change the pressure?
faq.a: No. Liquid pressure depends only on the depth and the density of the liquid, not on how wide the container is.
asks: Does a wide lake push harder than a narrow one?

facts: Each 10 m of water adds roughly one atmosphere (about 100 kPa) of pressure.
The Hoover Dam is about 200 m thick at its base and about 14 m thick at its top.

quiz.say: Where on a dam wall is the water pressure greatest?
quiz.show: Where on a dam wall is the water pressure greatest?
quiz.why: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth, so the bottom of the wall is pushed hardest.

wrong.0: The top has the least water above it, so pressure is lowest there.
wrong.2: Pressure grows with depth, so it is not equal.

quiz.say: About how much extra pressure does every 10 m of water add?
quiz.show: About how much extra pressure does every 10 m of water add?
quiz.why: 10 m of water presses about as hard as the whole atmosphere, roughly 100 kilopascals.

wrong.0: That would take about 100 metres of water.
wrong.1: 10 metres of water is heavy; it roughly doubles the pressure on you.
